result.title: SayWhen: Set-Valued Semantic Commitment for Low-Regret Early Speech
result.comment: Accepted at the NeurIPS 2026 Workshop PTA: From Pretrained Representations to Acting Agents
result.summary: Speaking early turns a prediction into an irreversible public commitment. We introduce SayWhen, a test-time controller that selects a task-directed act shared across typed continuation plans and controls its release as speech. A persistent veto blocks playback when intervening transcripts invalidate the candidate. We define regret-free early speech (RFES) to measure supported pre-endpoint releases without scored incompatibility. On a 72-prefix branching diagnostic, the generated-plan frontier attains 6.0% RFES with zero observed mean regret, versus 8.2% RFES and 0.068 regret for Matched Top-One. Measured planner latency constrains this path; a deterministic retail schema attains 31.7% RFES, compared with 32.0% for the complete policy. In a separate 30-task $τ$-Voice simulation, schema-derived candidates with cached text-to-speech (TTS) audio attain 21/30 task-level RFES. Eligible audio begins 1.51 seconds before the user-audio endpoint among the 22 tasks with early speech, or 1.11 seconds over all 30 tasks with zero for tasks without eligible early speech. Semantic veto and endpoint waiting each pass 16/30 tasks. Together, the studies demonstrate a controlled coverage-compatibility trade-off and schema-based pre-endpoint operation, making the supported public commitment an explicit unit of voice-agent control.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 SayWhen：一个测试时控制器，在语音代理中选取跨多种续写计划共享的任务行为，并持续否决被后续转录推翻的候选，以免过早播放；同时定义 RFES 指标，在分支诊断与 τ-Voice 模拟中衡量提前承诺的覆盖率与后悔。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「集合式候选—延后提交—新证据否决—后悔度量」框架可能启发 LVR 中 STOP 决策与答案提交时机的研究，尤其把不可逆公开承诺作为控制单元，可供核查提前输出的收益与代价权衡。
